title: I Made the Podcast Guest Keep the Off-the-Record Button

parts.text: I saw the red light still on after he said we were off record. I am twenty-six, freelance designer who got invited as a 'brand story.' The host, Cal, had a live laugh. The studio smelled like new foam and old coffee. I had told a story about my sister that was not for the internet. The engineer, Rae, looked at her shoes. Cal said, "Totally off record" I said, "The light is still red" My water bottle made a cheap crack when I set it down. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i. I counted three ceiling tiles with water stains before I spoke again. My socks had a hole I had been ignoring since Tuesday, which fit i.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The red light is on, my sister's story is in the buffer, and Rae is staring at her shoes.

parts.text: I asked Rae to delete the buffer in front of me. Cal said that would ruin flow. Rae deleted it anyway, because engineers have souls sometimes. I finished the interview about fonts, boring, safe. Cal tried to 'reconstruct from memory' in the edit. I sent a written refusal. The episode shipped without my sister. I still hate red LEDs. I put a sticky note on my own webcam: LIGHT MEANS REAL. Coffee-foam studios are not confessionals. My sister still does not listen to podcasts, which is luck. Rae said, "Buffer's gone" Cal said, "You're killing the vibe" Rae later freelanced with me on a real project. We used a checklist. It was sexy in a procedural way.
